- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.80) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above recent high for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.27) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model consistently overpredicts mid-term (10–20 day) prices when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; apply 1–3% downward adjustment for 10–20 day horizon.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3–5 days, model fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Mean reversion bias: if price is above 3σ from 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates by 1–3% when sentiment is high; apply 1–2% downward correction if sentiment >0.70 and price >80.00.
